query_text: Why do men have larger Adam's apples?

content.text:
Men typically have larger **Adam’s apples** because of **testosterone-driven changes during puberty**.

The “Adam’s apple” is the visible bump made by the **thyroid cartilage**, which surrounds and protects the **larynx**, or voice box. During male puberty, higher testosterone levels cause the larynx to grow larger. As it enlarges, the thyroid cartilage projects forward more noticeably, creating a bigger Adam’s apple.

This same growth also lengthens and thickens the vocal cords, which is why many boys’ voices deepen during puberty.

Women also have thyroid cartilage and can have visible Adam’s apples, but on average their larynx grows less during puberty, so the cartilage usually protrudes less.
